findings: P1 / must-fix — Fail closed when smoke-test ownership discovery fails — /Users/addomam/projects/amux-e03-build/tests/codex_native_smoke.rs:348-365 (particularly 349-355). Owned::cleanup records a failed discover() but continues sending SIGTERM/SIGKILL through the previous self.groups and self.known snapshots. Its preceding graceful-wait loop calls Child::try_wait(), so original children can already have been reaped; their PID/process-group numbers are then reusable. If /bin/ps fails or exceeds discover()'s one-second deadline, an unrelated process that has reused a recorded number passes group_alive()/getpgid() and receives the signal without any current birth/ownership validation. The watchdog also enters this cleanup path specifically after discovery failure. This new opt-in harness therefore violates the non-waived only-owned cleanup boundary on its failure path. Minimal correction: never perform PID/group fallback signaling using stale snapshots after discovery failure; preserve the cleanup error and signal only independently revalidated owned identities (or unreaped direct children), with current ownership validation before each fallback signal.
